effects: Runs only by delegatecall in the signer's Safe, and only while the Safe nonce is 0 (during Safe setup).
On any chain except chain 1, it replaces the Safe's singleton (its implementation code) with l2Singleton and emits ChangedMasterCopy.
No tokens or native value move; the function is not payable.
formats.shown: The screen says "Setup Safe L2" and shows the l2Singleton address under the label "Module".

findings.title: setupToL2 labels the new Safe singleton (implementation) as "Module", which is a different kind of right.
findings.evidence: SafeToL2Setup.sol setupToL2: `singleton = l2Singleton; emit ChangedMasterCopy(l2Singleton);`. Descriptor field: {"path": "l2Singleton", "label": "Module", "format": "addressName"}.
findings.fix: Change the label to "New Safe implementation (L2 singleton)".

findings.title: The setupToL2 intent "Setup Safe L2" does not say that it replaces the Safe's implementation code.
findings.evidence: SafeToL2Setup.sol setupToL2: `if (chainId() != 1) { singleton = l2Singleton; ... }`. Descriptor intent: "Setup Safe L2".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Switch Safe to L2 implementation" and add interpolatedIntent "Switch Safe implementation to {l2Singleton}".

findings.title: setupToL2 changes nothing on chain 1, but the chain 1 deployment shows the same setup intent.
findings.evidence: SafeToL2Setup.sol setupToL2: `if (chainId() != 1)` guards the only state write. Descriptor deployments include chainId 1.

findings.title: setupToL2 reverts unless called by delegatecall, so the descriptor applies only as nested calldata from Safe setup.
findings.evidence: SafeToL2Setup.sol: `modifier onlyDelegateCall() { require(address(this) != SELF, ...) }` and `onlyNonceZero` require `nonce == 0`. The descriptor binds the library address as a direct target.

setupToL2(address l2Singleton).worst: setupToL2 labels the new Safe singleton (implementation) as "Module", which is a different kind of right.
